method.title: How it is calculated
method.p1: The Sun and planets come from Keplerian orbital elements with the main Jupiter–Saturn perturbations. The Moon uses the 60-term lunar series from Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms. Rahu is the mean lunar node. Positions are converted to sidereal with the Lahiri ayanamsa, and the Lagna is solved from local sidereal time and latitude.
method.p2: Checked against the Swiss Ephemeris on 3,000 dates from 1900 to 2100: Moon within about 1′, Lagna within 1′, other grahas within 3½′. Houses are whole-sign. Yogas and doshas follow the rules shown on each card; traditions differ on cancellations.

p: A Janma Kundali (birth chart) is a map of the sky at the exact moment and place of your birth. It shows the Lagna (the sign rising in the east), the twelve bhavas (houses) and the positions of the nine grahas in the twelve rashis and twenty-seven nakshatras.
Jyotish reads this map to understand temperament, strengths and challenges, and uses the Vimshottari dasha system to time the main periods of life.

Your birth time is converted to Universal Time using the time zone history of your birth place. The positions of the Sun, Moon and planets are then computed from orbital mathematics and converted to the sidereal zodiac with the Lahiri ayanamsa, the standard used by the Government of India's calendar.
The Lagna is solved from local sidereal time and your latitude. Yogas, doshas and strengths are then checked with stated classical rules, so you can see why each result appears.

static.faqLede: Answers to common questions about Kundali and how this site works.

faq.a: A Kundali, or Janma Kundali, is a Vedic birth chart: the positions of the Sun, Moon, planets, Rahu and Ketu at the moment of your birth, arranged in twelve houses from the Lagna (ascendant). It is the basis of all Jyotish readings.

faq.q: What details do I need to make my Kundali?
faq.a: Your date of birth, exact time of birth and place of birth. The place gives latitude, longitude and time zone, which are needed to calculate the Lagna and houses correctly.

faq.q: What if I don't know my exact birth time?
faq.a: Planet signs and most nakshatras will still be correct, because they change slowly. The Lagna changes about every two hours and the Lagna degree about every four minutes, so house positions and dasha dates depend on an accurate time.

Planet positions are calculated with astronomical formulas and were tested against the Swiss Ephemeris for 1900 to 2100. The Moon and Lagna agree within about one arc-minute, and the other planets within about three and a half arc-minutes.
It uses the Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa, the standard adopted by the Indian Calendar Reform Committee and used by most Indian astrologers and panchangs.

Mangal dosha is present when Mars sits in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house. Grahavani checks it from the Lagna, the Moon and Venus. Many traditions also apply cancellation rules, so discuss important decisions with an astrologer.

Vimshottari is a 120-year cycle of planetary periods. Your starting period depends on the nakshatra of the Moon at birth. Each mahadasha is divided into nine antardashas, and Grahavani lists the dates for 100 years.

faq.q: Why do I need to log in, and is my data private?
faq.a: Your first Kundali is free with no account. To make more Kundalis, create a free account. It takes a few seconds and needs no email verification. Each chart is saved to your account so you can open it later, with row-level security so only you can read it.

varga.title: Divisional charts (Vargas)
varga.lede: Each varga divides every sign into equal parts to look at one area of life in detail.

D2.name: Hora
D2.about: Hora splits each sign in two (Sun and Moon halves). It shows how wealth is earned and kept.

D3.name: Drekkana
D3.about: Drekkana divides each sign into three. It is read for siblings, courage and initiative.

D4.name: Chaturthamsha
D4.about: Chaturthamsha divides each sign into four. It is read for home, land, vehicles and fixed assets.

D7.name: Saptamsha
D7.about: Saptamsha divides each sign into seven. It is read for children and progeny.

D10.name: Dashamsha
D10.about: Dashamsha divides each sign into ten. It is the main chart for career, status and achievements.

D12.name: Dwadashamsha
D12.about: Dwadashamsha divides each sign into twelve. It is read for parents and ancestry.

D16.name: Shodashamsha
D16.about: Shodashamsha divides each sign into sixteen. It is read for vehicles, comforts and happiness.

D20.name: Vimshamsha
D20.about: Vimshamsha divides each sign into twenty. It is read for worship, mantra and spiritual progress.

D24.name: Chaturvimshamsha
D24.about: Chaturvimshamsha divides each sign into twenty-four. It is read for education and learning.

D30.name: Trimshamsha
D30.about: Trimshamsha uses five unequal parts ruled by Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury and Venus. It is read for misfortunes and health troubles.

D60.name: Shashtiamsha
D60.about: Shashtiamsha divides each sign into sixty half-degrees. It is very sensitive to birth time and is read for karma from past lives.

p: Panchang means "five limbs". Every day is described by its tithi (lunar day), vara (weekday), nakshatra (Moon's star), yoga (Sun–Moon combination) and karana (half tithi). Together they are used to choose good times for work, travel, ceremonies and fasting.

Sunrise and sunset are computed for the city you choose. Each element's end time is found by solving for the exact moment the Moon and Sun reach the next boundary. Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda and Gulika are one-eighth parts of the daytime, and Choghadiya splits day and night into eight parts each.

Hindu festivals follow the lunar calendar. A festival is kept on the day its tithi is present at the right time — sunrise for most, midday for Ram Navami, evening for Diwali and midnight for Janmashtami and Shivaratri. Because these moments depend on your location, dates can differ by a day between cities and from printed calendars.

Months here are named in the Amanta system (month ends at new moon), used in Gujarat, Maharashtra and South India. In North India the Purnimanta system ends the month at full moon, so the month name for Krishna paksha dates is one month ahead; the festival dates themselves are the same.

Each sign's reading counts where the nine grahas are today from that Moon sign and applies the classical gochar (transit) rules: for example Jupiter is favourable in the 2nd, 5th, 7th, 9th and 11th, and Saturn in the 3rd, 6th and 11th. The Moon's house sets the mood of the day.
Vedic astrology reads the daily horoscope from your Moon sign (Rashi), not the western Sun sign. Make your free Kundali to find your Rashi — the site then highlights it here automatically.

Ashtakoot compares the two Moon nakshatras across eight kootas: Varna, Vashya, Tara, Yoni, Graha Maitri, Gana, Bhakoot and Nadi. Their points add up to 36. Traditionally 18 or more is acceptable and 25 or more is good.

Nadi and Bhakoot carry the most points, and a zero in either is called a dosha. Classical texts list cancellations, such as the Moon-sign lords being friends. Mangal dosha is checked from the Lagna, Moon and Venus for both people.

Each nakshatra has four padas, and each pada has a sacred first syllable (Akshar). Naming the child with that syllable is the traditional Namkaran practice. The names here start with your child's syllables; pick a pada to narrow the list.

The name number is the sum of the letters in the Chaldean system, reduced to one digit. Moolank comes from the day of birth and Bhagyank from the full date. A name whose number is friendly with these is marked lucky.

A muhurta is chosen from the tithi, nakshatra, weekday, yoga and karana. Each purpose has its own favourable stars and lunar days — for example Rohini, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta and Revati for marriage. Harsh yogas, Vishti karana and Rahu Kaal are avoided.

Marriage and griha pravesh are traditionally not held during Chaturmas, Kharmas (Sun in Dhanu or Meena), Adhika maas, Pitru Paksha, Holashtak, or while Jupiter or Venus is combust. Add your own Kundali to also skip days with bad Tara bala or Chandrashtama.

japa.h: How to use the mala counter
p: Choose a mantra and the number of malas for today, then tap the bead anywhere for each repetition. One mala is 108 repetitions; the larger bead (meru) marks the start.
Members who keep a mantra sadhana can pick it here: when today's goal is reached, the day is ticked in My Sadhana.
Traditionally a birthday is kept on the tithi (lunar day) of birth in the same lunar month. Because the lunar year is shorter than the solar year, that day moves on the civil calendar every year.
Shraddha is offered on the tithi of the ancestor's passing, at aparahna (afternoon), every year, and again in Pitru Paksha on the same tithi of the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada.
Prashna (horary astrology) casts a chart for the moment a sincere question is asked. The rising sign stands for the person asking; the house of the matter and its lord show the outcome.
The answer weighs the link between the Lagna lord and the lord of the matter, the Moon, benefics and malefics, and how the rising sign rises. Ask once, with a settled mind.
Pick a saved Kundali and the horoscope part fills itself: Rashi, Nakshatra and pada, Lagna, Manglik, Gana, Nadi and Varna, calculated with the same engine as the full report.
Your photo and details stay in this browser. Download the page as a PDF or share the summary on WhatsApp.

puja.h: How the puja muhurta is found
p: Each festival follows a time of day in the scriptures: Diwali in pradosh with a fixed (Vrishabha) lagna, Janmashtami at nishita (midnight), Ganesh Chaturthi at madhyahna, Dussehra at aparahna. We work out that window for your city.
The vidhi here is a simple home puja. Family and regional traditions differ — follow your elders or your priest where they guide you.
Ekadashi is broken the next morning (parana) after sunrise, once the first quarter of Dwadashi (Hari Vasara) is over and before Dwadashi ends — preferably in the first part of the morning.
Pradosh is kept until the evening puja after sunset; Sankashti Chaturthi until moonrise; Purnima until the next sunrise.
Sutak is observed only where the eclipse is visible: from 12 hours before a solar eclipse and 9 hours before a lunar eclipse begins. A penumbral lunar eclipse has no sutak.
Times are calculated for the city you choose. Each family chart shows the house from its Moon sign where the eclipse falls.

Grahavani uses the Indian numerology tradition: each number from 1 to 9 belongs to a planet (1 Sun, 2 Moon, 3 Jupiter, 4 Rahu, 5 Mercury, 6 Venus, 7 Ketu, 8 Saturn, 9 Mars). Names are counted with the Chaldean letter values, the method most used in India.

Mulank comes from the day you were born and shows your nature. Bhagyank is the total of the full birth date and shows the direction of your life. The name number shows how others meet you. A name or mobile number is lucky when its number is friendly to both your Mulank and your Bhagyank.

delivery.h: How the delivery muhurat is chosen
p: When a delivery is planned, the birth time can be chosen within the dates and hours the doctor allows. Jyotish then looks for a moment with a strong rising sign (lagna) and lagna lord, benefic planets in the angles and trines, and a well-placed Moon.

Slots in Rahu kaal or Yamaganda, on Amavasya or Rikta tithis, with the Moon in a Gandmool nakshatra or at a gandanta junction, or with Kaal Sarp yoga, score lower. The first dasha of life also counts.
Medical safety always comes first: only compare dates and times your doctor has approved.

In Jyotish a shop, firm or company is read from a chart cast for its 'birth': the moment it opened, was registered or made its first sale. The lagna is the business itself, the 2nd house cash and stock, the 7th customers and partners, the 10th reputation and growth, the 11th profit and the 6th competition and loans.

The business name is checked by Chaldean numerology against the opening date. Dasha periods of the lords of the 2nd, 10th and 11th are good for expansion; those of the 6th, 8th and 12th call for care.

Birth details you enter (name, date, time and place) are used to calculate your Kundali. If you create an account, we store your email, the Kundalis you make and a history of your entries so you can open them again.

Without an account, your history stays only in your own browser. A small cookie remembers that this browser has used its free Kundali. The details you type into the tools are also recorded in our activity log, described below.

Your data is used only to show your charts and history. We do not sell it or share it with advertisers. Share links show a chart only to people you give the link to, and you can turn a link off at any time.
Accounts and saved charts are stored with Supabase with row-level security, so each account can read only its own data. Pages are served by Vercel, which also records anonymous visit statistics.

We also keep an activity log of how the site is used: which pages and tools are opened and what is typed into them, such as names, birth dates, times and places, phone numbers and form fields, with the approximate city of your connection and, if you are logged in, your account email. This is kept whether or not you have an account. It helps us fix problems and improve the site, is visible only to the site administrator, never includes passwords or your IP address, and is deleted after 180 days.
You can delete any saved Kundali or history entry from your account at any time. To delete your account completely, contact us from your registered email.
Grahavani is a free tool for calculating Vedic astrology charts and related information. You may use it for personal purposes. Do not misuse the service or try to access other people's data.
Readings follow classical rules and are for guidance and interest only. They are not medical, legal, financial or psychological advice, and important decisions should not be based on them alone.

Positions are calculated mathematically and checked against standard ephemerides, but results depend on the accuracy of the birth details entered. Festival dates can differ by a day from other calendars because of location and tradition.
You are responsible for keeping your password safe. We may suspend accounts that abuse the service. These terms may be updated; the date at the top shows the latest version.

lp.phTitle: {g} in the {n} House – Effects in Vedic Astrology | Grahavani
lp.phDesc: Effects of {g} in the {n} house of the Kundali: what it means for {m}, when it is strong or weak, and its transit results.
lp.intro: {g} is the karaka (significator) of {kk}. The {n} house, called {hn} Bhava, shows {m}. When {g} sits here, these matters take on its colour.

ben: A benefic in the Lagna is a blessing: it gives a pleasant nature, good health and a likeable personality, and protects the whole chart.
In the 2nd house a benefic supports savings, a sweet and truthful way of speaking, and harmony in the family.
In the 3rd house a benefic makes one gentle in effort; it favours communication, writing and good relations with siblings, though drive may be soft.
In the 4th house a benefic brings a comfortable home, vehicles, a caring mother and peace of mind.
In the 5th house a benefic is excellent for intelligence, learning, creativity and children.
In the 6th house a benefic is somewhat weakened; it helps one serve others and settle disputes kindly, but can bring small health or debt matters.
In the 7th house a benefic supports a good spouse, happy partnerships and success in dealing with the public.
In the 8th house a benefic protects longevity and brings interest in research and hidden subjects, though its outward results are reduced.
In the 9th house a benefic is very fortunate: it brings luck, faith, higher learning and support from father and teachers.
In the 10th house a benefic brings respect, ethical work and a good name in one's career.
In the 11th house every graha gives gains; a benefic here brings steady income and helpful friends.
In the 12th house a benefic turns spending toward good causes and supports sleep, spiritual life and foreign connections.
mal: A malefic in the Lagna gives strength of will and drive, but can make one impatient or harsh and needs care for health.
In the 2nd house a malefic can make speech sharp and finances uneven, and calls for care in family relations.
In the 3rd house a malefic is at its best: it gives courage, initiative and the will to win through effort.
In the 4th house a malefic can disturb peace at home or with property, and asks one to build inner calm.
In the 5th house a malefic can delay children or unsettle the mind, while giving a sharp, practical intelligence.
In the 6th house a malefic is welcome: it defeats enemies, clears debts and gives the stamina to compete.
In the 7th house a malefic can bring friction or delay in marriage and partnerships, and calls for patience with others.
In the 8th house a malefic can bring sudden events and hidden worries, yet also resilience and depth.
In the 9th house a malefic can test faith or relations with father and teachers, and makes one follow one's own path.
In the 10th house a malefic gives ambition, authority and hard-won success in career.
In the 11th house a malefic is strong: it brings gains, fulfilment of desires and influential contacts.
In the 12th house a malefic can raise expenses, losses or sleep trouble, but also helps detachment and work abroad.

manglik.name: Mangal Dosha
manglik.what: Mars in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house from the Lagna or Moon. Tradition links it to friction and delay in marriage.
do: Recite the Hanuman Chalisa on Tuesdays and offer sindoor to Hanumanji.
Fast on Tuesdays and donate red lentils (masoor) and jaggery.
Chant “Om Angarakaya Namah” 108 times a day.
Match charts carefully before marriage — Mangal dosha in both charts balances out.

kaalsarp.name: Kaal Sarp Yoga
kaalsarp.what: All seven grahas sit on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis.
do: Chant the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra 108 times a day.
Offer milk and water on the Shivling on Mondays, especially in Shravan.
Have a Kaal Sarp shanti puja done once at a temple such as Trimbakeshwar or Ujjain.
Feed birds and serve snakes' shrines (Nag devta) on Nag Panchami.

sadesati.name: Sade Sati
sadesati.what: Saturn is passing the sign before, on, or after your Moon — a 7½-year period of hard work and lessons.
do: Light a sesame-oil lamp under a peepal tree on Saturday evenings.
Recite the Hanuman Chalisa or Shani Chalisa on Saturdays.
Donate black sesame, mustard oil, black urad or blankets on Saturdays.
Stay honest, patient and kind to workers and elders — Saturn rewards discipline.

dhaiya.name: Shani Dhaiya
dhaiya.what: Saturn is passing the 4th or 8th sign from your Moon — a 2½-year phase of strain.
do: Chant “Om Sham Shanaishcharaya Namah” 108 times on Saturdays.
Offer mustard oil to Shani Dev on Saturdays and light a lamp.
Serve or donate to elderly and labouring people.

pitra.name: Pitra Dosha
pitra.what: The Sun or the 9th house is touched by Rahu, Ketu or Saturn — read as unfinished duties to the ancestors.
do: Offer water and black sesame to the ancestors (tarpan) on Amavasya.
Do shraddha in Pitru Paksha and feed cows, crows, dogs and the needy.
Water a peepal tree and light a lamp there on Saturdays.
Respect and serve your parents and elders.

grahan.name: Grahan Yoga
grahan.what: {g} shares a sign with Rahu or Ketu, which can cloud confidence or peace of mind.
do: Chant the Gayatri mantra daily, or “Om Som Somaya Namah” for the Moon.
Offer water to the rising Sun every morning.
Chant mantras during eclipses and donate after them.
Keep a daily routine of meditation or pranayama.

guruchandal.name: Guru Chandal Yoga
guruchandal.what: Jupiter shares a sign with Rahu or Ketu, which can cloud judgement and guidance.
do: Chant “Om Brim Brihaspataye Namah” 108 times on Thursdays.
Respect teachers, elders and guides and seek their blessings.
Donate chana dal, turmeric and yellow cloth on Thursdays.
Worship Lord Vishnu and read the Vishnu Sahasranama.

kemadruma.name: Kemadruma Yoga
kemadruma.what: No graha sits beside the Moon (2nd or 12th from it) or in a kendra from it, which can bring loneliness or money worries.
do: Worship Lord Shiva on Mondays with milk and water.
Chant “Om Namah Shivaya” 108 times a day.
Wear white on Mondays and keep a silver item with you.
Donate rice, milk or white cloth on Mondays.

shrapit.name: Shrapit Yoga
shrapit.what: Saturn and Rahu share a sign — linked with delays that ask for patience.
do: Chant the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra on Saturdays.
Donate black sesame and blankets to the poor on Saturdays.
Light a sesame-oil lamp at a Shani or Hanuman temple.
Have a shanti puja done once, if your priest advises it.

Sun: Offer water to the rising Sun from a copper vessel.
Float a copper coin in flowing water on a Sunday.
Respect your father and avoid accepting things for free.
Moon: Keep a silver item with you and drink water from a silver glass.
Take your mother's blessings before important work.
Keep a small pot of water by your bed at night and pour it on a plant in the morning.
Mars: Float sweet batashe or revri in flowing water on Tuesdays.
Give red lentils (masoor dal) in charity.
Keep good relations with brothers and avoid anger.
Mercury: Feed green fodder to a cow on Wednesdays.
Respect sisters, daughters and aunts and give them gifts.
Float a copper coin with a hole in flowing water.
Jupiter: Apply a saffron or turmeric tilak on the forehead.
Serve elders and teachers; offer chana dal at a temple on Thursday.
Water a peepal tree (do not touch it on Saturday).
Venus: Feed a cow and give white things such as curd or rice in charity.
Respect your spouse and keep the home clean and fragrant.
Wear clean, ironed clothes and use perfume.
Saturn: Feed crows and offer mustard oil in charity on Saturday.
Help labourers and servants; never insult them.
Rahu: Keep a solid square piece of silver with you.
Float coconut or barley in flowing water.
Keep good relations with in-laws; avoid blue clothes.
Ketu: Feed a dog, especially a two-coloured one.
Give a black-and-white blanket in charity.
Respect your maternal uncle and keep good ties with your son.

diwali.about: Lakshmi puja on Kartik Amavasya welcomes prosperity; Ganesha is worshipped first.
diwali.samagri: Lakshmi–Ganesha idols, red cloth, kalash with water, coins, rice, kumkum, haldi, flowers and lotus, sweets, diyas with ghee, incense, camphor, betel leaves, puffed rice (kheel) and batashe.
vidhi: Clean the house and draw rangoli at the door.
Place a red cloth on a raised seat with the idols and a kalash.
Worship Ganesha first, then Lakshmi with kumkum, rice, flowers and sweets.
Chant Om Shreem Mahalakshmyai Namah and offer kheel and batashe.
Do aarti, light diyas all over the home and share prasad.
katha: When Lord Rama returned to Ayodhya after fourteen years, the people lit rows of lamps to welcome him.
On this night Goddess Lakshmi visits clean, lit homes and blesses them with wealth.
So families clean the house, light lamps and pray for prosperity and harmony.

dhanteras.about: Dhanvantari and Lakshmi are worshipped two days before Diwali; buying metal is auspicious.
dhanteras.samagri: A new utensil or coin, Dhanvantari or Lakshmi picture, diyas, kumkum, rice, flowers, sweets and a lamp for Yama.
vidhi: Clean the home and the entrance.
In the evening worship Dhanvantari and Lakshmi with flowers and sweets.
Place the new utensil or coin before the deity.
Light a lamp facing south outside the door for Yama (Yama Deepam).
Pray for health and prosperity and do aarti.
katha: Dhanvantari, the physician of the gods, rose from the churning of the ocean carrying the pot of nectar on this day.
A king's son was saved from death when his wife kept lamps burning and gold at the door all night.
So people light a lamp for Yama and pray for long, healthy lives.

ganeshChaturthi.about: Ganesha's birthday on Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi; the murti is installed at madhyahna.
ganeshChaturthi.samagri: Ganesha murti, red cloth, durva grass (21 blades), modak, red flowers, kumkum, haldi, rice, coconut, betel leaves, incense and diya.
vidhi: Install the murti on a clean seat facing east or north.
Invoke Ganesha (avahana) and do prana pratishtha with mantras.
Offer durva, red flowers, kumkum and 21 modak.
Chant Om Gan Ganapataye Namah and read the Ganesha katha.
Do aarti morning and evening until visarjan.
katha: Goddess Parvati shaped a boy from sandalwood paste and asked him to guard her door.
Shiva, not knowing him, cut off his head; to console Parvati he gave the boy an elephant's head.
Shiva blessed him to be worshipped first in every ritual as Ganesha, the remover of obstacles.

janmashtami.about: Krishna's birth at midnight on Bhadrapada Krishna Ashtami; devotees fast until midnight.
janmashtami.samagri: Bal Gopal idol, cradle, panchamrit, Ganga jal, new clothes and flute, tulsi, butter and mishri, fruits, flowers and diya.
vidhi: Fast through the day and decorate the cradle.
At midnight bathe Bal Gopal with panchamrit and Ganga jal.
Dress the idol and place him in the cradle.
Offer butter, mishri and tulsi; chant Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya.
Rock the cradle, sing bhajans and break the fast with prasad.
katha: King Kansa imprisoned his sister Devaki because her eighth child was foretold to kill him.
Krishna was born at midnight; the prison doors opened and Vasudeva carried him across the Yamuna to Gokul.
He grew up with Yashoda and Nanda and later freed Mathura from Kansa.

mahaShivaratri.about: The great night of Shiva; worship continues through the four prahars of the night.
mahaShivaratri.samagri: Shivalinga, water and milk, curd, honey, ghee, bilva leaves, dhatura, white flowers, sandalwood, bhasma, incense and diya.
vidhi: Fast and keep the mind on Shiva through the day.
In each prahar do abhishek with water, milk, curd, honey and ghee.
Offer bilva leaves, dhatura and white flowers.
Chant Om Namah Shivaya through the night.
Break the fast the next morning after puja.
katha: On this night Shiva and Parvati were married.
A hunter, sitting in a bilva tree all night, unknowingly dropped leaves and water on a Shivalinga and was freed of his sins.
So a night of wakeful worship on Shivaratri is said to bring great merit.

navratri.about: Nine nights of the Goddess, beginning with ghatasthapana in the morning of Ashvin Shukla Pratipada.
navratri.samagri: Kalash, barley seeds and soil, coconut with red cloth, mango leaves, red chunari, Durga picture, akhand diya, kumkum, flowers and fruits.
vidhi: Sow barley in soil and set up the kalash with mango leaves and coconut (ghatasthapana).
Light the akhand diya to burn for nine days.
Each day worship one form of Durga with flowers and kumkum.
Read Durga Saptashati or chant Om Dum Durgayai Namah.
On Ashtami or Navami feed and honour young girls (kanya puja).
katha: The demon Mahishasura could not be defeated by the gods.
Their combined power took form as Goddess Durga, who fought him for nine days.
On the tenth day she destroyed him — the victory of good over evil.

holikaDahan.about: The bonfire on Phalguna Purnima evening, the night before Holi.
holikaDahan.samagri: Wood and cow-dung cakes, raw cotton thread, water, roli, rice, flowers, coconut, new grain (wheat or barley) and sweets.
vidhi: Gather at the Holika pyre in the evening.
Wrap raw cotton thread around it three or seven times.
Offer water, roli, rice, flowers and coconut.
Light the fire in the muhurta and roast new grain in it.
Walk around the fire and pray for protection.
katha: King Hiranyakashipu wanted his son Prahlad to stop praying to Vishnu.
His sister Holika, who could not be burnt, sat in a fire holding Prahlad.
By Vishnu's grace Holika burnt and Prahlad came out unharmed.

rakshaBandhan.about: Sisters tie a rakhi on Shravan Purnima, avoiding Bhadra; the afternoon is preferred.
rakshaBandhan.samagri: Rakhi, thali with roli, rice, diya, sweets and water.
vidhi: Prepare the thali with roli, rice, diya and sweets.
Apply tilak on the brother's forehead.
Tie the rakhi on his right wrist.
Do aarti and offer sweets.
The brother gives a gift and promises protection.
katha: When Krishna cut his finger, Draupadi tore her sari and tied it round the wound.
Krishna promised to protect her, and saved her honour in the Kaurava court.
The rakhi carries the same promise of love and protection.

karwaChauth.about: Married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for their husband's long life.
karwaChauth.samagri: Karwa (clay pot) with water, sieve, diya, sargi, roli, rice, sweets, Karwa Chauth katha book and a picture of Gauri.
vidhi: Eat sargi before sunrise and keep a nirjala fast.
In the evening worship Gauri and the karwa and listen to the katha.
At moonrise look at the moon through a sieve.
Offer water (arghya) to the moon.
Break the fast with water from the husband's hands.
katha: Queen Veeravati broke her fast early when her brothers showed her a false moon.
Her husband fell ill; she kept the fast faithfully the next year.
By the Goddess's grace her husband recovered, and the fast has been kept ever since.

ramNavami.about: Rama's birth at madhyahna on Chaitra Shukla Navami.
ramNavami.samagri: Rama Darbar picture, cradle, panchamrit, tulsi, yellow flowers, fruits, kheer or panjiri, diya and Ramcharitmanas.
vidhi: Fast in the morning and clean the puja place.
At madhyahna bathe the idol and place Ram Lalla in the cradle.
Offer tulsi, yellow flowers and kheer.
Chant Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram or read the Ramayana.
Do aarti and share prasad.
katha: King Dasharatha of Ayodhya had no children and performed a yajna.
Rama was born to Kaushalya at noon on Navami.
He grew to be maryada purushottam, the ideal of dharma.

hanumanJayanti.about: Hanuman's birth is celebrated on Chaitra Purnima with sindoor and Hanuman Chalisa.
hanumanJayanti.samagri: Hanuman picture, sindoor with jasmine oil, red flowers, betel leaves, laddoo or boondi, diya and Hanuman Chalisa.
vidhi: Bathe early and fast or eat simply.
Offer sindoor mixed with jasmine oil to Hanuman.
Offer red flowers, betel leaves and laddoo.
Read Hanuman Chalisa or Sundarkand.
Do aarti and pray for strength and courage.
katha: Anjana and Kesari were blessed with a son through the wind god Vayu.
As a child Hanuman leapt to swallow the rising Sun, thinking it a fruit.
He became Rama's greatest devotee and carried the message to Sita in Lanka.

dussehra.about: Vijayadashami, the victory of Rama over Ravana; Shami and weapon puja at aparahna.
dussehra.samagri: Shami leaves, roli, rice, flowers, sweets, diya, and books or tools for Ayudha puja.
vidhi: Worship Goddess Aparajita and the Shami tree.
Clean and worship tools, books and vehicles.
Exchange Shami leaves as 'gold' with elders and friends.
Watch or perform Ravana dahan in the evening.
Seek the blessings of elders.
katha: Ravana carried Sita away to Lanka.
After a long battle Rama killed Ravana on the tenth day.
Vijayadashami marks the victory of dharma and of good over evil.

sharadPurnima.about: The brightest full moon of the year; kheer is kept in moonlight at night.
sharadPurnima.samagri: Kheer in a silver or clay bowl, white flowers, Lakshmi picture, diya and a white cloth.
vidhi: Worship Lakshmi in the evening.
Make kheer and keep it under the moonlight, covered with a thin cloth.
Stay awake and chant (Kojagari jagran).
Offer arghya to the moon.
Eat the kheer as prasad in the morning.
katha: On this night Lakshmi moves across the earth asking 'Ko jagarti?' — who is awake?
She blesses those who are awake and worshipping.
The moon is said to pour nectar into the kheer kept in its light.

vasantPanchami.about: Saraswati puja on Magha Shukla Panchami; yellow clothes and books are honoured.
vasantPanchami.samagri: Saraswati picture, yellow cloth and flowers, books and pens, yellow sweets, kumkum, rice and diya.
vidhi: Wear yellow and set up Saraswati on a yellow cloth.
Place books, pens and instruments before her.
Offer yellow flowers, kumkum and yellow sweets.
Chant Om Aim Saraswatyai Namah.
Children begin learning letters (akshar abhyasam).
katha: Brahma created the world but found it silent.
Saraswati appeared with the veena and gave the world speech and music.
So on Vasant Panchami knowledge and the arts are worshipped.

rk.about2: Because sunrise and sunset change with the season and the city, Rahu Kaal is different in every city and on every day. Yamaganda and Gulika are two more inauspicious parts of the day calculated the same way.

ch.fq3: What is the difference between choghadiya and hora?

fa.holi: Holi, the festival of colours, is played on the day after Holika Dahan, on Phalguna Krishna Pratipada, celebrating spring and the victory of devotion over arrogance.
fa.ugadi: Ugadi and Gudi Padwa mark the Hindu lunar new year on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada; the new samvatsara begins and families eat a mix of six tastes.
fa.chaitraNavratri: Chaitra Navratri is the spring Navratri, nine nights of Durga worship that begin on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada and end with Ram Navami.
fa.mahavirJayanti: Mahavir Jayanti celebrates the birth of Bhagwan Mahavir, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, on Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi.
fa.akshayaTritiya: Akshaya Tritiya, Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya, is one of the most auspicious days of the year: anything begun, bought or given today is said never to diminish.
fa.buddhaPurnima: Buddha Purnima, the full Moon of Vaishakha, remembers the birth, enlightenment and passing of Gautama Buddha.
fa.nirjalaEkadashi: Nirjala Ekadashi, in Jyeshtha Shukla, is the strictest Ekadashi, kept without even water; keeping it is said to equal all 24 Ekadashis of the year.
fa.rathYatra: Rath Yatra is the chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra in Puri, on Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya.
fa.devshayaniEkadashi: Devshayani Ekadashi, Ashadha Shukla Ekadashi, is when Lord Vishnu goes to sleep for the four months of Chaturmas; weddings pause until Dev Uthani Ekadashi.
fa.guruPurnima: Guru Purnima, the full Moon of Ashadha, honours teachers and Maharishi Ved Vyasa.
fa.nagPanchami: Nag Panchami, Shravana Shukla Panchami, is the day of worship of the serpent deities with milk and flowers.
fa.anantChaturdashi: Anant Chaturdashi, Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturdashi, is the worship of Lord Anant (Vishnu) and the day of Ganesh visarjan.
fa.pitruPakshaStart: Pitru Paksha is the fortnight of remembering ancestors with shraddha and tarpan; it begins after Bhadrapada Purnima and ends on Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
fa.durgaAshtami: Durga Ashtami, the eighth day of Sharad Navratri, is the day of Maha Gauri worship and kanya pujan in many homes.
fa.govardhanPuja: Govardhan Puja, the day after Diwali, remembers Krishna lifting Govardhan hill; an Annakut of many dishes is offered.
fa.bhaiDooj: Bhai Dooj, Kartika Shukla Dwitiya, is when sisters pray for their brothers' long life and brothers give gifts.
fa.chhathPuja: Chhath Puja, Kartika Shukla Shashthi, is the worship of the Sun god and Chhathi Maiya with arghya at sunset and at sunrise the next day.
fa.devUthaniEkadashi: Dev Uthani (Prabodhini) Ekadashi, Kartika Shukla Ekadashi, is when Lord Vishnu wakes from his four-month sleep; Tulsi Vivah follows and the wedding season begins.
fa.kartikPurnima: Kartik Purnima, also Dev Deepawali, is the full Moon of Kartika, celebrated with holy baths and lamps; it is also Guru Nanak Jayanti.
fa.gitaJayanti: Gita Jayanti, Margashirsha Shukla Ekadashi, marks the day Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna; it is also Mokshada Ekadashi.
fa.makarSankranti: Makar Sankranti is the day the Sun enters Makara (Capricorn), celebrated as Uttarayan, Pongal, Lohri and Khichdi with kite flying, sesame sweets and charity.
fa.meshaSankranti: Mesha Sankranti, the Sun's entry into Mesha, is the solar new year: Baisakhi in Punjab, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, Vishu in Kerala and Pohela Boishakh in Bengal.

nkt: Ashwini natives are quick, energetic and pioneering, with a healer's touch and a love of new beginnings. They act fast, help others readily and dislike waiting, though patience and follow-through are lessons for them.
Bharani gives strong will, passion and the capacity to carry heavy responsibility. These natives are creative and determined, live life intensely, and learn to handle extremes with self-control.

Krittika is sharp and fiery, like a blade that cuts through confusion. Its natives are honest, direct, protective and ambitious, with high standards; a softer word can serve them better than a sharp one.

Rohini, the Moon's favourite, gives charm, beauty, creativity and a love of comfort and growth. These natives are attractive, artistic and fertile in ideas, and do well in anything that nurtures or creates.

Mrigashira is the searching star: curious, gentle, intelligent and always looking for something new. Its natives are good communicators and researchers, though restlessness can keep them moving from one thing to the next.

Ardra brings intensity, intellect and transformation, like a storm that clears the air. Its natives are sharp thinkers and hard workers who grow through difficulty and are drawn to research and technology.
Punarvasu is the star of renewal: optimistic, generous and wise, always able to return to light after hardship. Its natives are content with simple living, forgiving, and natural teachers.
Pushya is considered the most auspicious nakshatra: nourishing, protective, disciplined and devoted. Its natives are responsible, caring and spiritual, and often take care of family and community.

Ashlesha gives depth, sharp intelligence and strong intuition, with a hypnotic, persuasive quality. Its natives understand people well and are skilled strategists; trust and openness are their lessons.
Magha is the throne of the ancestors: dignified, proud and generous, with respect for tradition and lineage. Its natives have natural authority and leadership and a strong sense of honour.
Purva Phalguni is the star of pleasure, rest and creativity. Its natives are warm, charming, affectionate and artistic, enjoy life and relationships, and bring people together.
Uttara Phalguni gives kindness, reliability and a sense of duty in partnerships. Its natives are generous helpers and good organisers who keep their promises and value lasting relationships.
Hasta, the hand, gives skill, cleverness and a practical, resourceful mind. Its natives are good with their hands and words, humorous and hard-working, and can turn ideas into results.
Chitra, the bright jewel, gives a love of beauty, design and craftsmanship. Its natives are creative, stylish and charismatic, with talent for architecture, art and anything that is built well.

Swati, the independent shoot moved by the wind, gives flexibility, diplomacy and a love of freedom. Its natives are fair-minded, good at business and trade, and thrive when free to find their own way.
Vishakha is the star of purpose: determined, ambitious and focused on a goal until it is reached. Its natives are energetic and capable of great achievement, and learn to balance drive with patience.
Anuradha gives devotion, friendship and the ability to succeed far from home. Its natives are loyal, organised and cooperative, keep good company, and can be very disciplined.
Jyeshtha is the eldest: responsible, protective and capable, with natural seniority. Its natives are courageous and resourceful, often carry family burdens, and are wise when they use power gently.
Mula, the root, goes to the bottom of things. Its natives are searching, philosophical and investigative, unafraid to break down what no longer works in order to find the truth.
Purva Ashadha is the invincible star: confident, persuasive and full of enthusiasm. Its natives are idealistic and influential, recover quickly, and believe strongly in what they do.
Uttara Ashadha gives lasting victory through right effort. Its natives are principled, patient, responsible and fair, with leadership that grows steadily and earns respect.
Shravana is the star of listening and learning. Its natives are attentive, knowledgeable and devoted, gather wisdom from others, and make good teachers, counsellors and communicators.
Dhanishta gives wealth, rhythm and musical talent. Its natives are ambitious, generous and good in groups, with a gift for music, sport and organising events.
Shatabhisha, the hundred healers, gives independence, secrecy and a scientific, healing mind. Its natives are thoughtful and private, drawn to medicine, research and unconventional ideas.
Purva Bhadrapada gives intensity, idealism and spiritual fire. Its natives are passionate about their causes, can be very generous, and go through deep transformations.
Uttara Bhadrapada gives depth, calm and wisdom, like still deep water. Its natives are patient, self-controlled, compassionate and good at counselling, with a strong inner life.
Revati, the last nakshatra, is gentle, kind and protective, guiding travellers safely to their destination. Its natives are compassionate, creative and spiritual, and care for the weak.

rst: Mesha Moon gives an active, courageous and direct mind that loves to lead and start new things. Feelings are quick and honest, anger rises fast and fades fast, and the native thrives on challenge and independence.

Vrishabha is the Moon's exaltation sign, giving a calm, steady and patient mind. These natives value security, comfort, beauty and good food, are loyal and practical, and can be very determined once decided.

Mithuna Moon gives a curious, witty and restless mind that loves conversation, learning and variety. These natives are adaptable and social, good with words and trade, but need focus to finish what they start.

Karka is the Moon's own sign: sensitive, caring and deeply attached to home, mother and family. Emotions run deep, memory is strong, and the native nurtures others, though moods can change like the tides.

Simha Moon gives a proud, generous and warm-hearted mind with natural dignity and a wish to be respected. These natives are confident leaders and loyal friends, and shine when they can create and be appreciated.
Kanya Moon gives an analytical, careful and service-minded nature. These natives notice details, love order and health, are practical and modest, and need to beware of worry and over-criticism.
Tula Moon gives a balanced, refined and diplomatic mind that seeks harmony and partnership. These natives are fair, artistic and sociable, dislike conflict, and can take time to make up their minds.

Vrishchika is the Moon's debilitation sign, giving intense, private and powerful emotions. These natives are perceptive, determined and loyal, feel deeply, and have great capacity for transformation and research.

Dhanu Moon gives an optimistic, philosophical and freedom-loving mind. These natives are honest, generous and fond of travel, learning and religion, and inspire others with their faith and enthusiasm.
Makara Moon gives a serious, disciplined and ambitious mind. These natives are practical, patient and hard-working, take responsibility early, and build success slowly and surely.

Kumbha Moon gives an independent, humanitarian and original mind. These natives think about society and ideas, value friendship and fairness, and can seem detached while caring deeply about the larger good.

Meena Moon gives a gentle, imaginative, intuitive and compassionate nature. These natives are artistic and spiritual, forgive easily, and need a calm environment and some boundaries to protect their sensitivity.

manglik.title: Manglik dosha
manglik.seoTitle: Manglik Dosha (Mangal Dosha) – Meaning, Effects, Cancellation & Remedies
manglik.desc: What Manglik dosha is, how it is checked, when it is cancelled, and the traditional remedies.
what: Manglik (Mangal or Kuja) dosha is formed when Mars sits in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house of the birth chart. Mars is a fiery planet, and in these houses it is believed to affect marriage and married life.
It is very common: roughly half of all charts have Mars in one of these houses when counted from the Lagna, Moon or Venus, so having it is not unusual.
check: Mars is checked from three points: the Lagna, the Moon and Venus. When Mars is in one of the six houses from the Lagna it is strongest; from the Moon or Venus it is milder. South Indian tradition usually counts the 2nd house; some North Indian traditions use only 1, 4, 7, 8 and 12.
effects: Traditionally it is linked with delays in marriage, disagreements, a dominating temperament, or stress in married life. In practice its effect depends on Mars's sign, strength and aspects and on the whole chart.
cancel: Classical texts give many cancellations: Mars in its own sign (Mesha, Vrishchika) or exalted (Makara); Mars in Karka or Simha for some houses; Jupiter or Venus in the Lagna or aspecting Mars; Mars conjunct the Moon or Jupiter; and when both partners are Manglik, the dosha balances.
Many astrologers also consider it weaker after the age of 28.
remedies: Worship of Hanuman, reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and fasting on Tuesdays; chanting the Mangal mantra; donating red lentils (masoor) on Tuesdays; and, traditionally, marrying another Manglik or performing Kumbh Vivah before marriage.

kaal-sarp.title: Kaal Sarp dosha
kaal-sarp.seoTitle: Kaal Sarp Dosha – Meaning, 12 Types, Effects & Remedies
kaal-sarp.desc: What Kaal Sarp dosha is, its 12 types, how it is checked, and the traditional remedies.
what: Kaal Sarp dosha (or yoga) is formed when all seven planets, from the Sun to Saturn, lie on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis. Rahu is the head of the serpent and Ketu the tail, and the planets are said to be held between them.
check: The positions of all planets are compared with Rahu and Ketu. If every planet falls within the arc from Rahu to Ketu (or Ketu to Rahu), the yoga is present. If even one planet is outside, it is partial or absent.
There are 12 named types according to the house of Rahu: Anant, Kulik, Vasuki, Shankhpal, Padma, Mahapadma, Takshak, Karkotak, Shankhachud, Ghatak, Vishdhar and Sheshnag.
effects: It is associated with struggle, delays and sudden ups and downs, especially in the dashas of Rahu and Ketu. It is not mentioned in the oldest classical texts, and many famous, successful people have it; its effect depends on the rest of the chart.
cancel: It is considered weak or cancelled when a planet is conjunct Rahu or Ketu in the same degree range, when strong benefics are in kendras, or when Rahu is in a favourable house such as the 3rd, 6th or 11th.
remedies: Kaal Sarp puja at Trimbakeshwar or Ujjain; worship of Lord Shiva and offering milk on Mondays and Nag Panchami; chanting the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra; and chanting the Rahu and Ketu mantras.

sade-sati.title: Shani Sade Sati
sade-sati.seoTitle: Shani Sade Sati – Meaning, Three Phases, Effects & Remedies
sade-sati.desc: What Sade Sati is, its three phases, how it affects each sign, and the traditional remedies.
what: Sade Sati is the seven-and-a-half-year transit of Saturn over the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from your Moon sign. Each phase lasts about two and a half years. It returns roughly every 30 years, so most people go through it two or three times.
check: Rising phase (Saturn in the 12th from the Moon): expenses, travel, sleep and changes in surroundings. Peak phase (Saturn over the Moon): pressure on the mind, health and personal life, but also maturity. Setting phase (Saturn in the 2nd): family, money and speech, with gradual relief.
effects: It is a period of hard work, responsibility and karmic lessons. For people whose charts have a strong or well-placed Saturn, or whose Lagna is ruled by Venus or Saturn, it often brings success and stability. Its result also depends on the dasha running.
cancel: It is milder when Saturn is exalted, in its own sign or a yogakaraka in your chart, when Jupiter aspects the Moon, or when a favourable dasha is running.
remedies: Worship Hanuman and Lord Shiva; recite the Hanuman Chalisa or Shani Stotra on Saturdays; light a sesame-oil lamp under a peepal tree; donate black sesame, mustard oil, iron or black cloth on Saturdays; and serve the elderly, workers and the needy.

pitru.title: Pitru dosha
pitru.seoTitle: Pitru Dosha – Meaning, Signs in the Chart & Remedies
pitru.desc: What Pitru dosha is, how it is seen in a chart, and the traditional remedies such as shraddha and tarpan.
what: Pitru dosha is understood as unresolved karma or unfulfilled wishes of one's ancestors that show in the birth chart. It is a traditional reason given for repeated obstacles in family matters, children or progress.
check: It is commonly linked with the Sun (father) afflicted by Rahu, Ketu or Saturn, especially in the 9th house (ancestors, father, fortune), or with Rahu in the 9th or 5th. An afflicted 9th lord is also considered.
effects: Traditionally linked with delays in marriage or children, family disputes, and effort not giving full results. As with every dosha, it must be judged with the strength of the whole chart.
cancel: It is milder when Jupiter aspects the Sun or the 9th house, when the 9th lord is strong, or when benefics occupy the 9th house.
remedies: Perform shraddha and tarpan in Pitru Paksha and on Amavasya; offer water to the Sun daily; feed cows, crows, dogs and Brahmins; plant and water a peepal tree; recite the Pitru Stotra; and perform Narayan Bali or Tripindi Shraddha at a tirtha such as Gaya, Trimbakeshwar or Haridwar.

ru.desc: {n} mukhi rudraksha is ruled by {p} and blessed by {d}: benefits, mantra, who should wear it and how.

rut: One mukhi rudraksha is the form of Lord Shiva himself and is rare. It is worn for spiritual focus, concentration, leadership and freedom from fear, and is linked with the Sun.
Two mukhi rudraksha represents Ardhanarishvara, the union of Shiva and Shakti. It is worn for harmony in relationships and marriage, emotional balance and peace of mind, and is linked with the Moon.
Three mukhi rudraksha represents Agni, the fire god. It is worn to burn away past karma, guilt and low confidence, and for energy and self-belief; it is linked with Mars.
Four mukhi rudraksha represents Brahma, the creator. It is worn for knowledge, memory, speech and creativity, and is especially good for students and writers; it is linked with Jupiter.
Five mukhi rudraksha represents Kalagni Rudra and is the most common bead. It is worn for health, calm, blood pressure balance and general well-being, and suits everyone; it is linked with Jupiter.
Six mukhi rudraksha represents Kartikeya. It is worn for willpower, emotional stability, charm and success in the arts and relationships, and is linked with Venus.
Seven mukhi rudraksha represents Mahalakshmi. It is worn for wealth, prosperity and relief from financial difficulty, and is linked with Saturn.
Eight mukhi rudraksha represents Lord Ganesha. It removes obstacles and brings success in new ventures and clear thinking, and is linked with Rahu.
Nine mukhi rudraksha represents Goddess Durga. It is worn for courage, energy, protection and fearlessness, and is linked with Ketu.
Ten mukhi rudraksha represents Lord Vishnu. It is worn for protection from negative energy, legal troubles and fears, and for peace at home; it is linked with Mercury.
Eleven mukhi rudraksha represents Hanuman (the eleven Rudras). It is worn for courage, confidence, leadership and protection while travelling, and is linked with Mars.
Twelve mukhi rudraksha represents Surya, the Sun god. It is worn for authority, vitality, leadership and success in administration, and is linked with the Sun.
Thirteen mukhi rudraksha represents Kamadeva. It is worn for attraction, charm, fulfilment of desires and success in creative work, and is linked with Venus.
Fourteen mukhi rudraksha, the 'deva mani', represents Hanuman and Shiva. It is worn for intuition, wise decisions and protection, and is linked with Saturn.

mean.mercury: Budh rules speech, contracts, trade, travel and devices. When it is retrograde, communication tends to be misread, plans slip and old matters return. It is a good time to revise, repair and reconnect, and a weak time to sign new contracts or buy electronics.
mean.venus: Shukra rules love, marriage, beauty, art and luxuries. Retrograde Shukra brings old relationships and feelings back for review, and judgement about money and pleasure is less reliable. Marriage muhurats are traditionally avoided while it is retrograde.
mean.mars: Mangal rules energy, courage, property, surgery and conflict. Retrograde Mangal turns that energy inward: frustration, delays in property and legal matters, and quarrels that flare and return. Effort works better on unfinished tasks than on new fights.
mean.jupiter: Guru rules wisdom, children, teachers, money and dharma. Retrograde Guru slows outer growth but deepens inner learning; promises made earlier get reviewed. A good time for study, spiritual practice and finishing pending blessings.
mean.saturn: Shani rules work, discipline, delay and karma. Retrograde Shani returns to unfinished duties; past karmic lessons come back and old debts or tasks demand completion. Patience and honest work are rewarded more than shortcuts.

do.mercury: Back up data, read every document twice and avoid signing big contracts or buying gadgets if you can. Chant the Budh mantra on Wednesdays and finish old work.
do.venus: Avoid starting a marriage or buying luxury items; review relationships and spending calmly. Worship Lakshmi on Fridays and keep things simple.
do.mars: Avoid surgery that can wait, property disputes and rash driving. Channel energy into exercise. Hanuman Chalisa on Tuesdays helps.
do.jupiter: Revisit studies, spiritual practice and old plans for children or money. Respect teachers and elders; recite the Guru mantra on Thursdays.
do.saturn: Clear pending duties and debts, be patient with delays and serve the needy. Light a sesame oil lamp on Saturdays.

rt.note: Sun, Moon, Rahu and Ketu are never retrograde in the usual sense; Rahu and Ketu always move backwards.

sun.about: Surya mahadasha lasts six years and puts the soul, ego, father, government and authority in focus. It is a time to stand on your own and be seen.
sun.good: With a strong Sun (in Mesha, Simha, or in houses 1, 9, 10, 11) it brings promotion, government favour, recognition, leadership and good health.
sun.bad: With a weak or afflicted Sun it can bring ego clashes, trouble with the father or bosses, heart, eye or bone complaints and loss of reputation.

moon.about: Chandra mahadasha lasts ten years and colours life through the mind, mother, home, emotions and public life. Mood and peace of mind decide the results.
moon.good: A strong, waxing Moon gives peace, comfort, a good home, travel, popularity, fame with the public and steady income.
moon.bad: A weak or afflicted Moon brings anxiety, mood swings, sleep problems, worries about the mother and fluctuating finances.

mars.about: Mangal mahadasha lasts seven years and brings energy, courage, property, siblings and competition to the front. Things move fast.
mars.good: A strong Mars gives land and property, success in sports, police, army, engineering and surgery, courage and victory over rivals.
mars.bad: An afflicted Mars brings anger, accidents, injuries, disputes over property, quarrels with siblings and blood-related complaints.

mercury.about: Budh mahadasha lasts seventeen years and rewards intellect, speech, trade, writing and learning. It is often a period of education and business.
mercury.good: A strong Mercury gives success in studies, business, accounts, media and communication, a sharp mind and good friends.
mercury.bad: An afflicted Mercury brings nervousness, skin problems, trouble in trade or contracts, and misunderstandings.

jupiter.about: Guru mahadasha lasts sixteen years and is usually one of the most blessed periods: wisdom, children, marriage, teachers and wealth grow.
jupiter.good: A strong Jupiter brings marriage, children, higher studies, respect, wealth, spiritual growth and good advisers.
jupiter.bad: A weak Jupiter can bring liver or weight problems, wrong advice, delays with children and overconfidence in money.

venus.about: Shukra mahadasha is the longest, twenty years, and brings love, marriage, comforts, vehicles, art and beauty into life.
venus.good: A strong Venus gives a happy marriage, luxury, vehicles, a beautiful home, success in art, fashion and entertainment.
venus.bad: An afflicted Venus brings relationship trouble, overspending, indulgence, and kidney or reproductive complaints.

saturn.about: Shani mahadasha lasts nineteen years. It tests and then rewards: hard work, discipline and patience build lasting results.
saturn.good: A well-placed Saturn (yogakaraka for Vrishabha and Tula lagna, or in houses 3, 6, 10, 11) gives a stable career, authority, property and long-term success.
saturn.bad: A badly placed Saturn brings delays, heavy responsibility, chronic illness, loneliness and setbacks that need patience.

rahu.about: Rahu mahadasha lasts eighteen years and brings sudden rises, foreign links, technology, ambition and unconventional paths.
rahu.good: A well-placed Rahu (in houses 3, 6, 10, 11) gives sudden success, foreign travel or settlement, fame, politics and gains through technology.
rahu.bad: An afflicted Rahu brings confusion, fears, deception, addiction, legal trouble and sudden losses.

ketu.about: Ketu mahadasha lasts seven years and turns the mind inward: detachment, spirituality, research and endings that make room for new beginnings.
ketu.good: A well-placed Ketu gives spiritual progress, insight, research skill, healing ability and freedom from old burdens.
ketu.bad: An afflicted Ketu brings confusion, sudden separations, hidden illness, accidents and a feeling of loss.

gajakesari.about: Gajakesari means 'elephant and lion'. It forms when Guru (Jupiter) is in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house) from the Moon, and is one of the most quoted yogas for good fortune.
gajakesari.effects: It gives intelligence, respect, a good name that lasts, help from influential people and steady prosperity. People with it often become advisers, teachers or leaders.
gajakesari.strong: It works fully when Jupiter and the Moon are strong, not combust or debilitated, and not with Rahu or Ketu. A Jupiter in Makara or an afflicted Moon reduces the results.

budhaditya.about: Budhaditya yoga forms when Budh (Mercury) and Surya (Sun) are in the same sign. Because Mercury is always close to the Sun, it is very common; its strength decides how much it gives.
budhaditya.effects: It gives a sharp intellect, good speech, skill in study, accounts, writing and administration, and recognition for intelligence.
budhaditya.strong: It is strongest in houses 1, 4, 5, 9 or 10 and when Mercury is not combust (more than about 14° from the Sun). In houses 6, 8 or 12, or with Mercury combust, it gives less.

raj.about: Raj yoga forms when the lord of a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) and the lord of a trikona (1, 5, 9) join, aspect each other or exchange signs. It unites effort (kendra) with fortune (trikona).
raj.effects: It gives rise in status, authority, wealth and recognition, often during the dasha of the planets that form it.
raj.strong: It is strongest when the planets are well placed and strong, and gives results mainly in their dasha or antardasha. If they also rule 6, 8 or 12, or are debilitated or combust, the yoga weakens.

yogakaraka.about: A yogakaraka is a single planet that rules both a kendra and a trikona from the lagna, so it forms a Raj yoga on its own. Saturn for Vrishabha and Tula, Mars for Karka and Simha, and Venus for Makara and Kumbha are yogakarakas.
yogakaraka.effects: Its dasha is usually one of the best periods of life: career rise, property, status and fulfilment of ambitions.
yogakaraka.strong: It works best when the yogakaraka is strong, in a good house and not afflicted. A debilitated or combust yogakaraka still helps, but with effort and delay.

chandramangal.about: Chandra-Mangal yoga forms when the Moon and Mars are together or aspect each other. It joins the mind with energy and drive.
chandramangal.effects: It is known as a wealth yoga: business sense, earning through property, trade or bold ventures, and a determined nature.
chandramangal.strong: It is best when both are strong and in good houses. It can also make one hot-tempered or impatient, especially if Mars is afflicted.

ruchaka.about: Ruchaka yoga is one of the five Pancha Mahapurusha yogas. It forms when Mangal is in its own sign (Mesha, Vrishchika) or exalted (Makara) in a kendra from the lagna.
ruchaka.effects: It gives courage, a strong body, leadership, success in army, police, sports, engineering or surgery, and the ability to defeat rivals.
ruchaka.strong: It is strongest in the 10th or 1st house and when Mars is not combust or with Saturn or Rahu.

bhadra.about: Bhadra yoga is a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga formed when Budh is in its own sign (Mithuna) or exalted (Kanya) in a kendra from the lagna.
bhadra.effects: It gives a brilliant intellect, excellent speech, skill in business, writing, law or accounting, and a youthful look.
bhadra.strong: It is strongest when Mercury is not combust and is free from malefic influence.

hamsa.about: Hamsa yoga is a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga formed when Guru is in its own sign (Dhanu, Meena) or exalted (Karka) in a kendra from the lagna.
hamsa.effects: It gives wisdom, righteousness, respect, a spiritual nature, good children and prosperity. Such people are often teachers, advisers or judges.
hamsa.strong: It is strongest when Jupiter is not combust or with Rahu, and when its dasha runs in life.

malavya.about: Malavya yoga is a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga formed when Shukra is in its own sign (Vrishabha, Tula) or exalted (Meena) in a kendra from the lagna.
malavya.effects: It gives beauty, charm, a happy marriage, vehicles, luxury, artistic talent and enjoyment of life.
malavya.strong: It is strongest when Venus is not combust and free from Saturn, Rahu or Ketu's affliction.

sasa.about: Shasha yoga is a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga formed when Shani is in its own sign (Makara, Kumbha) or exalted (Tula) in a kendra from the lagna.
sasa.effects: It gives authority over many people, success in politics, administration, mining, land or labour-related work, and long-lasting results from hard work.
sasa.strong: It is strongest in the 10th house and when Saturn is not combust. Its results often come after age 36.

vipreet.about: Vipreet Raj yoga forms when the lords of the dusthanas (6, 8, 12) sit in another dusthana, for example the 6th lord in the 8th or 12th. One problem cancels another.
vipreet.effects: It gives sudden success after difficulty, gains from the fall of rivals, and the ability to rise in crisis.
vipreet.strong: It works best when the dusthana lords are not also lords of good houses and are not strong in a way that harms the lagna.

adhi.about: Adhi yoga forms when benefics (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) occupy the 6th, 7th and 8th houses from the Moon.
adhi.effects: It gives leadership, a comfortable life, good health, victory over enemies and a position of trust.
adhi.strong: It is strongest when all three benefics take part and are strong; with only one or two the effect is milder.

sunapha.about: Sunapha yoga forms when a planet other than the Sun is in the 2nd house from the Moon.
sunapha.effects: It gives self-earned wealth, good reputation, intelligence and a contented mind.
sunapha.strong: Benefics in the 2nd from the Moon give the best results; malefics give wealth through effort and struggle.

anapha.about: Anapha yoga forms when a planet other than the Sun is in the 12th house from the Moon.
anapha.effects: It gives a pleasing personality, good health, comforts and a spiritual leaning in later life.
anapha.strong: Benefics in the 12th from the Moon give the best results.

durudhara.about: Durudhara yoga forms when planets other than the Sun occupy both the 2nd and the 12th houses from the Moon.
durudhara.effects: It gives wealth, vehicles, servants, generosity and fame; the Moon is well supported on both sides.
durudhara.strong: It is best with benefics on both sides; it also cancels Kemadruma yoga.

kemadruma.about: Kemadruma yoga forms when no planet (other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu) is in the 2nd or 12th house from the Moon, and none is in a kendra from it. The Moon is left alone.
kemadruma.effects: It can bring loneliness, money worries, mental restlessness and a feeling of lack of support, even in a good family.
kemadruma.strong: It is cancelled when a planet is in a kendra from the lagna or the Moon, when the Moon is strong and full, or when Jupiter aspects the Moon. Most charts that show it have some cancellation.

grahan.about: Grahan yoga forms when the Sun or the Moon is joined with Rahu or Ketu in the same sign. The luminary is 'eclipsed' by the shadow planet.
grahan.effects: With the Sun it can affect confidence, the father and reputation; with the Moon it can bring anxiety, confusion and mood swings.
grahan.strong: It is milder when the luminary is far in degrees from the node or strong by sign. Remedies are chanting the Surya or Chandra mantra and worship on eclipse days.

guruchandal.about: Guru Chandal yoga forms when Jupiter is joined with Rahu (and by some authors Ketu) in the same sign.
guruchandal.effects: It can distort judgement and values, bring wrong advice or teachers, and trouble with children or education, though it can also give unconventional wisdom.
guruchandal.strong: It is milder when Jupiter is strong by sign (own or exalted). Worship of Guru on Thursdays and respecting teachers is the classical remedy.

shakata.about: Shakata yoga forms when the Moon is in the 6th, 8th or 12th house from Jupiter. Like a cart wheel, fortune rises and falls.
shakata.effects: It can bring ups and downs in money and status, and periods of struggle after good times.
shakata.strong: It is cancelled when the Moon is in a kendra from the lagna or when Jupiter is strong. Many charts with it do well after the late thirties.

matching.q: How many gunas are needed for marriage?
matching.a: 18 out of 36 is the usual minimum in Ashtakoota milan; 24 or more is considered very good. Bhakoot and Nadi dosha matter more than the total, and both have classical exceptions that this tool checks.

matching.q: What is Nadi dosha and can it be cancelled?
matching.a: Nadi dosha means both have the same Nadi (Aadi, Madhya or Antya), which scores 0 out of 8. It is cancelled when both have the same rashi but different nakshatras, the same nakshatra but different rashis, or the same nakshatra in different padas.
Yes. Mangal dosha is checked from the lagna, Moon and Venus for both, along with the common cancellations, and the result says whether it is present in one, both or neither.

panchang.q: What are the five parts of the panchang?
panchang.a: Tithi (lunar day), vara (weekday), nakshatra (Moon's star), yoga and karana. Together they describe the quality of the day.

panchang.q: Why is panchang different for each city?
panchang.a: Sunrise, sunset, Rahu Kaal and the moment a tithi or nakshatra is in force at sunrise depend on where you are, so the panchang is computed for your city.
Rahu Kaal is a period of about 90 minutes each day, different for each weekday, considered unsuitable for starting new work. It is one eighth of the daytime.

calendar.q: How are Hindu festival dates decided?
calendar.a: Each festival follows a tithi and a time of day: for example Diwali needs Amavasya during pradosh kaal, and Janmashtami needs Ashtami at midnight. The date is the day on which that tithi covers that time in your city.

calendar.q: Why can a festival fall on different dates in different cities?
calendar.a: Sunrise and the tithi timing differ by place, so when a tithi changes close to sunrise or the key time, cities can observe the festival on different days.

calendar.q: Does the calendar use Purnimanta or Amanta months?
calendar.a: Month names follow the Amanta system (month ends on Amavasya), used in Gujarat, Maharashtra and South India. In the Purnimanta north Indian system the Krishna paksha belongs to the next month's name.

rashifal.q: Is this rashifal based on the Moon sign?
rashifal.a: Yes. Vedic rashifal is read from your Moon sign (rashi), not the Sun sign used in western horoscopes.

rashifal.q: How is the daily rashifal calculated?
rashifal.a: From the actual position of every planet on that day, counted from your Moon sign (gochar), using the classical favourable houses for each planet.
When the transiting Moon is in the 8th sign from your Moon sign, for about two and a half days a month. It is a time to avoid big decisions and arguments.

names.q: How do I find a baby name by nakshatra?
names.a: Each nakshatra pada has a starting syllable. Choose the baby's nakshatra and pada (or pick a saved kundali) and the tool lists names starting with that syllable.
Moolank is the reduced birth date (day) and Bhagyank the reduced full date of birth. A name number friendly to both is considered lucky in Chaldean numerology.

names.q: Can I check a name I already like?
names.a: Yes. Type it in the 'check a name' box to see its name number, ruling planet and whether it suits the Moolank and Bhagyank.

muhurta.q: How is a shubh muhurat chosen?
muhurta.a: By checking tithi, nakshatra, weekday, yoga and the lagna at that time for the activity, and avoiding Rahu Kaal, bhadra and other faults. The tool scores every window of every day.
Yes. Adding your birth details also checks tara bala and chandra bala, so the dates suit your own nakshatra and Moon sign.

muhurta.q: Which months are avoided for marriage?
muhurta.a: Traditionally when Guru or Shukra is combust, during Kharmas (Sun in Dhanu or Meena) and in Chaturmas in many communities. The marriage muhurat already leaves these out.

puja.a: Each festival has a prescribed time: Lakshmi puja in pradosh with a fixed (sthir) lagna, Ganesh puja at midday, Janmashtami at midnight. Puja in that window is considered most fruitful.

puja.q: Can I do puja without a priest?
puja.a: Yes. The guides give a simple home puja: samagri, step-by-step vidhi and the katha. Follow your family custom where it differs.

puja.q: Is the muhurat the same in every city?
puja.a: No. It depends on local sunset, sunrise or moonrise, so choose your city to get the right time.

vrat.q: When should I break the Ekadashi fast?
vrat.a: On the next day after sunrise, once the first quarter of Dwadashi (Hari Vasara) is over and before Dwadashi ends, preferably in the morning. The tracker shows this parana window.

vrat.q: When is the Pradosh vrat puja done?
vrat.a: In the evening twilight after sunset (pradosh kaal), on Trayodashi. The tracker shows the window for your city.

vrat.q: When is the Sankashti fast broken?
vrat.a: After seeing the Moon on Krishna Chaturthi. The moonrise time for your city is shown for each Sankashti.

eclipses.a: Only where the eclipse is visible: 12 hours before a solar eclipse and 9 hours before a lunar eclipse. A penumbral lunar eclipse has no sutak.

eclipses.q: Does an eclipse affect my rashi?
eclipses.a: The effect is read from the house the eclipse falls in from your Moon sign; houses 3, 6, 10 and 11 are usually fine, while 1, 4, 8, 12 or the janma nakshatra call for japa.
A planet seems to move backwards from Earth for some weeks. Its matters turn inward and delays are common; the list shows when each planet turns retrograde and direct.

japa.a: A mala has 108 beads; 108 is a sacred number linked to the 27 nakshatras times 4 padas. One round of the mala is one unit of japa.
The mantra of your weak planet or running mahadasha lord, or the deity you follow. Your kundali report suggests the mantra for each planet.

japa.q: Does the counter save my progress?
japa.a: Yes, rounds are saved on your phone, and with an account they appear in your sadhana streaks.

tithi.a: The Hindu birthday falls on the same tithi in the same lunar month every year, so its date changes in the English calendar.

tithi.q: How is the shraddha date found?
tithi.a: Shraddha is done on the tithi of death in Pitru Paksha, or on the same tithi and month each year. Enter the date and city to get the coming dates.
Yes. With an account you can save people and ancestors and get a reminder the day before.

prashna.q: How should I ask the question?

numerology.q: How do I find my Mulank and Bhagyank?
numerology.a: Mulank is your day of birth reduced to one digit (the 28th gives 2 + 8 = 10 → 1). Bhagyank is every digit of your full date of birth added and reduced to one digit. The calculator does both and adds your name number.

numerology.q: Which numerology system does Grahavani use?
numerology.a: The Indian system with Chaldean letter values: each number from 1 to 9 belongs to a planet, and the letters of a name have values from 1 to 8.

numerology.q: How do I know if my mobile number is lucky?
numerology.a: Add all the digits of the number and reduce the total to one digit. The number is lucky when that digit is friendly to both your Mulank and your Bhagyank. Type it into the mobile number check.

mobFaq.q: Which mobile number total is the luckiest?
mobFaq.a: There is no single lucky total; it depends on your Mulank and Bhagyank. Totals 1, 3, 5 and 6 are friendly to many numbers, and 5 suits almost everyone.

mobFaq.q: Should I change my mobile number?

1.trait: Mulank 1 is ruled by the Sun. You are born to lead: independent, confident and full of ideas, you prefer to start things rather than follow. You value respect and self-made success.
1.strong: Leadership, willpower, originality, honesty and the courage to take decisions.
1.weak: Ego, stubbornness, impatience and difficulty taking advice or sharing control.
1.career: Government service, management, politics, own business, medicine and any role with authority.
1.love: Loyal and protective, but needs a partner who respects their independence. Gets on well with 2, 3 and 9.
1.health: Watch the heart, eyes, blood pressure and back; regular sunlight and rest help.
1.destiny: Bhagyank 1 points to a life of leadership and self-reliance. Success comes from your own efforts, often after the age of 22 to 25, and you are meant to start new things, lead people and earn a name.
1.py: A year of new beginnings: start projects, take charge and plant seeds for the next nine years.

2.trait: Mulank 2 is ruled by the Moon. You are gentle, caring and imaginative, with strong intuition and a gift for bringing people together. Your mood changes like the Moon.
2.strong: Kindness, diplomacy, creativity, intuition and loyalty to family.
2.weak: Over-sensitivity, mood swings, indecision and worrying too much.
2.career: Arts, music, writing, nursing, hospitality, counselling, dairy, water and import-export trades.
2.love: Romantic and devoted; needs emotional security. Gets on well with 1, 3 and 5.
2.health: Watch digestion, water retention, sleep and stress; a calm routine helps.
2.destiny: Bhagyank 2 gives a life built on partnership and service. You do best working with others, in roles that need care, tact and imagination, and peace at home is the key to your progress.
2.py: A year of patience and partnership: cooperate, build relationships and let plans ripen slowly.

3.trait: Mulank 3 is ruled by Jupiter. You are wise, disciplined and optimistic, a natural teacher and advisor who likes to grow and help others grow. Principles matter to you.

3.weak: Bossiness, pride in being right, and taking on too much.
3.career: Teaching, law, finance, banking, religion, consulting and administration.
3.love: Sincere and responsible partner who expects respect. Gets on well with 1, 2 and 9.

3.destiny: Bhagyank 3 brings a life of learning and guidance. Respect, children and wealth grow through knowledge, ethics and helping others.

4.trait: Mulank 4 is ruled by Rahu. You think differently, question rules and work hard behind the scenes. Life brings sudden changes, but you are practical and keep building.

4.weak: Rebelliousness, suspicion, sudden decisions and a habit of making enemies.

5.strong: Intelligence, communication, humour, adaptability and business sense.
5.weak: Restlessness, impatience, nervousness and starting more than you finish.
5.career: Business, trade, sales, marketing, media, writing, accounts, IT and travel.

5.destiny: Bhagyank 5 brings a life of movement, trade and communication. Opportunities come through travel, people and business, and your luck grows when you use your speech and wit.

6.weak: Love of luxury, overspending, jealousy and avoiding hard conversations.

7.weak: Detachment, secrecy, restlessness and difficulty expressing feelings.

socad.reelsLede: Pick the day the reel is for — today, tomorrow, the day after, next week or any future date. Daily reels use that day, the weekly reel the 7 days from it and the festival reel the 14 days from it. The special-day reel shows what is special that day (festival, vrat, eclipse, Sarvartha Siddhi or Pushya yoga, planets changing sign or turning retrograde) and the precautions (Bhadra, Panchak, Rahu Kaal, Chandrashtama) with remedies. Each language builds up line by line, slides to a detail card, then swipes to the next language. Made here in your browser; nothing is saved on the server.
